The nickel-base single crystal superalloy PWA 1480 is a candidate blading material for the advanced turbopump development (ATD) program of the space shuttle main engine (SSME).

In advanced liquid propellent rocket engines such as the SSME, the turbine blades are subjected to severe thermal gradients, both along the span and through the thickness during startup and shutdown cycles, as well as centrifugal and vibratory loads.
The single crystal superalloy PWA 1480 is grown along the low modulus [001] crystal orientation by a directional solidification process.
Unless a seed crystal is used during the solidification process, the secondary crystal orientation [010] tends to be randomly oriented with respect to the geometry of the turbine blade.

Cubic single crystal materials such as PWA 1480 exhibit anisotropic elastic behavior, so the stresses developed within the single crystal superalloy due to mechanical and thermal loads are likely to be affected by the exact orientation of the secondary crystallographic direction.

The effects of secondary crystal orientation on the elastic response of single crystal PWA 1480 superalloy were investigated using a square plate with a side length of 25.4 mm and a thickness of 3.2 mm.

The elastic stresses developed within the single crystal PWA 1480 plate were computed with elastic finite-element stress analysis for each combination of loading condition and secondary orientation angle.
The commercially available MARC code was used to conduct the elastic stress analyses, and the finite-element model of the square plate consisted of 500 8-noded, isoparametric elements.
The elastic stiffness matrices for different secondary orientation angles were computed using the simplified method of Liebermen and Zirinsky.

The temperature-dependent elastic constants and the thermal coefficient of expansion for single crystal PWA 1480 were determined by the engineering division of Pratt & Whitney, United Technologies Corporation under the NASA Lewis Research Center Contract NAS3-23939.

For the case involving a thermal gradient through the thickness of the square plate, the secondary orientation angle of 0° minimized thermal stresses, whereas the secondary orientation angle of 45° maximized the thermal stresses.
The variations in the stress components with the secondary orientation angle were dependent on the type of loading (mechanical, thermal, or combined) imposed on the square plate.
At 38°C, the elastic stiffness coefficients of PWA 1480 single crystal were: C11 = 250 GPa, C12 = 163 GPa, and C44 = 129 GPa.
The imposed thermal gradients along the Z-axis and X-axis of the square plate were provided, with temperatures ranging from 400°C to 800°C.
The study investigated the elastic stresses developed within a few selected elements in the finite-element mesh under mechanical, thermal, and combined thermal and mechanical loads.
